paragraphs: Yochanan ben Yehonatan, Aryeh of Kefar Shichya.

Hyman says that in Yevamot 122b he testified before R' Tarfon about a man who had been killed, and Tarfon permitted the wife to remarry on that testimony. The description ‘an incident involving a certain man’ suggests to Hyman that he was not a Torah scholar.

notes.text: The consulted Yevamot account names Yochanan Aryeh as the man who later fell ill and died; another man testified about him. Hyman describes the entry’s subject as the witness and the death as a killing. Those substantive differences remain held, without rewriting the frozen source.

Hyman’s witness/killed account remains explicitly his: earlier Yevamot122b evidence instead named Yochanan Aryeh as the deceased and a different witness, not an automatic correction of Hyman’s narrative. Aryeh’s attachment and the village spelling remain questions. The complete notice contains the wife’s remarriage and Hyman’s inference that the man was not a Torah scholar; the old supposed missing continuation is withdrawn. No new whole primary paragraph was supplied for this entry, and Tarfon’s abbreviated title stays R'.

Printed Hyman (vol. II, p. 682) presents Yochanan as a witness about a killing. In both tellings in Yevamot 122b, another man testifies about Yochanan, who later fell ill and died. In the second telling, Rabbi Tarfon tests the order of Aryeh and the village name before accepting the testimony. Rashi explains that moving Aryeh would make it sound like a name for the village. In Tosefta Yevamot 14 the parallel accounts likewise distinguish the companion who speaks from Yochanan and give a variant village spelling. No consulted wording establishes the basis for Hyman’s different account or his inference about the man’s scholarship.
